encounters.cc: Recent weight loss and dietary habits concerning for eating disorder

lines: Recent weight loss and dietary habits concerning for eating disorder

The patient is an 18-year-old female with a known history of Kallmann syndrome and prior multidisciplinary evaluation for primary amenorrhea who presents for psychiatric assessment of recent weight loss and dietary changes.
She has lost 10 kg over the past 6 months and currently has a BMI of 17.
She reports that she became a vegetarian 8 months ago and insists that she is eating enough, although she avoids all animal products.
Her parents note that she has become increasingly preoccupied with her body image and spends several hours a day exercising.
She denies any binging, purging, or use of laxatives.

encounters.cc: Increasing preoccupation with healthy eating and excessive exercise despite illness

lines: Increasing preoccupation with healthy eating and excessive exercise despite illness

The patient is a 19-year-old female with Kallmann syndrome and a history of anorexia nervosa, restricting type, previously managed in Psychiatry and Gastroenterology, who presents for continued outpatient care.

Over the past year, she has become increasingly preoccupied with healthy eating and refuses to eat anything she deems "unclean" or "processed." She has eliminated entire food groups and often skips meals.
Her mother reports that the patient exercises excessively, even when sick or injured.
The patient is a competitive gymnast and says she's "just trying to stay fit." She has not had a menstrual period in over 4 months.

encounters.cc: Behavioral changes and secondary amenorrhea related to excessive fitness focus

lines: Behavioral changes and secondary amenorrhea related to excessive fitness focus
The patient is a 19-year-old female with Kallmann syndrome and a history of anorexia nervosa who returns for outpatient psychiatric follow-up with continued behavioral changes.
Over the past year, she has become increasingly focused on her physical fitness and diet.
She has eliminated several food groups from her meals and insists on eating alone.
She spends hours daily running or performing structured cardio routines at home.
Although she maintains straight A's in school, her teachers report she has withdrawn socially.
She has not had a menstrual period in over five months, which she attributes to stress and increased training.
